# Independent audit: complete midpoint-star certificate

Audited source: candidate 0c151a0c56ccc06f, including Section 7.



## 1. Actual body and the central certificate

The defining inequalities give a compact full five-dimensional convex polytope. Its 33 integer fibers are exactly \(r_kT\), all with positive four-volume; the endpoint radius is \(1/17\). Radius and translation interpolate affinely on each side of zero, so the body is exactly the hull of its integer fibers. The common translation changes the fiber center to \((|k|/17)v\), with the stated sign.

Each term of the central certificate is a valid pair contribution and concerns two distinct source fibers. The own term is the exact ordinary depth. Coordinate permutation averaging decreases every relevant gauge simultaneously because all pair centers lie on the same invariant axis.

For a nonnegative axis parameter, the vertex cap gives the own-depth upper bound, and the centered inner copy gives equality on the axis. For a negative averaged parameter, the maximum ordinary depth of a simplex bounds the own term by its centroid value, while every averaged pair gauge is at least its value at zero. These facts justify the reduction of all central-fiber points; no unsupported concavity of the entire certificate is used.

The gauge is \(a\) on \(av\) for \(a\ge0\), and \(-4a\) for \(a\le0\). This produces the two correct positive-part branches. Each branch is convex on every interval between consecutive pair centroids, so the finite endpoint maximum is exhaustive. The exact largest numerator is \(282546\), at \(t=3/17\), and the recorded positive target gap is correct.

## 2. Every integer anchor and every actual point

The upper comparison
\[
\Phi_d(r,s)\le2\Gamma_d((r+s)/2)^d
\]
is valid for the previously proved lower-bound function \(\Phi_d\). In the interpolation regime it follows from \(2(1-c)\le(d-1)c\); in the plateau regime from \(c(d+1)/2\ge1\). The source explicitly distinguishes this upper comparison from a generally false lower bound on actual caps.

For \(k\ge0\), all available reflected pairs have
\[
\rho_{k,h}=1-\max(k,h)/17,\qquad
m_{k,h}=(\max(k,h)/17)v,\qquad 1\le h\le16-k.
\]
This follows from \(|k-h|+|k+h|=2\max(k,h)\), and the displayed index range is exact.

After coordinate averaging, a point below the own centroid can be replaced by that centroid: the own simplex depth increases to its global maximum and all pair gauges decrease. For an axis point \(xv\) at or above that centroid, the exact own depth is \(\Gamma_4V(1-x)^4\). Such \(x\) lies in \([k/17,1]\), so it is also a legitimate central-fiber parameter.

The comparison for \(\Phi_4\) bounds each noncentral pair term by the same gauge expression used centrally. For \(h>k\), midpoint and radius agree exactly with central pair \(h\). For \(h\le k\), both terms equal \(2\Gamma_4V(1-x)^4\). Thus the noncentral envelope is termwise a subsum of the central certificate. All omitted central terms are nonnegative.

Reflection covers negative anchors. There are no other actual integer bases. Therefore the exact global certificate maximum equals the central one, attained at anchor zero and \(y=(3/17)v\). The statement makes no claim that unpaired fibers have zero actual cap mass.

## 3. Archived sampling theorem and independent OC safety

I independently compared Section 5 with Section 1 of one-fine-coordinate-height-sensitive-sampling-and-trapezoid-mass.md. Its hypotheses apply to the compact convex body \(Q\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^4\), lattice \(h\mathbb Z\), and every closed cap. The maximal four-dimensional fiber volume is exactly \(V\). Hence the permitted absolute error is \(hV\), not an error normalized by total volume, and no sample on a closed boundary is removed.

The ordinary volume is
\[
|Q|=V\,\frac25(1-h^5).
\]
Using the section centroid \(r g_T\), the first-moment integral gives each continuous centroid coordinate
\[
\frac16\frac{1-h^6}{1-h^5},
\]
while the base centroid is zero by reflection symmetry. This point lies in the actual sampled central fiber.

Ordinary five-dimensional Grünbaum followed by the signed lower discrepancy bound gives sampled weighted cap mass at least
\[
V(\Gamma_5W-h).
\]
Dividing by the exact total \(hM\) yields the recorded rational normalized bound, strictly exceeding \(\Gamma_4/2\). Scaling the base back is invertible and maps the actual sampled lattice to the original integer lattice while preserving all halfspaces. Thus this is an actual all-cap safety certificate, including pure base-normal caps.

## 4. Reinspection of the nonproduct reflection example

I also rechecked candidate ad68d9332c30d210 and audit-nonproduct-reflection-and-explicit-base-depth.md.

There is no omitted body-completion issue. The five-vertex integer polygon has exactly the twelve listed lattice points, and its positive affine radius makes every real fiber exactly the corresponding homothetic body. The same-shape interpolation realizes the full body as the hull of its integer fibers.

The explicit base \(j=(0,1)\) has weighted halfspace depth
\(H=B+C+2D+2E\) by the three normal-sign cases, with a matching cap of normal \((-4,1)\). In the ambient body, every selected fiber whose centroid lies in a cap contributes at least its ordinary Grünbaum fraction. This includes zero base normal, zero continuous normal, and all containing closed caps. The resulting actual point satisfies \(\Gamma_{14}H/M>\Gamma_{14}/4\). The separate own-cube-center certificate in the source is also valid.

No correction is required in either example. Both are failures of specified stronger lower certificates, accompanied by explicit actual OC-safe points.
